0.content:
While investigating rainforest ruins at Tighnari's invitation, Faruzan overheard someone praying earnestly to the Dendro Archon to learn words faster. She decided at once that this was a student of "suitable age, fitting direction, and excellent quality" and stepped out from behind a tree. Collei squeaked in fright, and Tighnari had to clear up the misunderstanding. Faruzan has wanted to teach her ever since. She brings Collei food at Gandharva Ville, tells her not to let Tighnari know, scolds Tighnari over Collei's eye bags, and calls her respectful, diligent and perfect. She does not quite realise what else draws her: Collei suffered terribly and still found the strength to face life.

Collei likes her and admits she is a brilliant scholar, but Faruzan's intensity and her ancient languages frighten her a little. Faruzan respects Collei's choices and has not pushed while she recovered. In 2023 Collei overheard Faruzan planning a surprise birthday party for her, "the grander the better". Collei later lent her a juicer from Sucrose, which Faruzan took over.

In the 6.1 Fieldwise Center event (limited), Collei coordinated consultants from every Darshan, and Faruzan praised her confidence and leadership above her own thesis-bound students. Faruzan's 2025 birthday letter, while claiming not to pry, asks the Traveler which light novels Collei likes.

1.content:
Tighnari treats Faruzan as a true senior researcher "in every sense of the word". He invited her to survey rainforest ruins, and in the 3.5 hangout he asked her to repair Karkata because Kshahrewar and Spantamad scholars were too prejudiced to trust. He tells the Traveler the story of her entrapment so that Faruzan doesn't have to, and warns that she doesn't want pity. She calls him "that brat", enjoys travelling with "the living copy of the Rainforest Survival Guide", and says he has eaten more kinds of fungi than she has.

In the 3.6 Extravaganza (limited) she named him the favourite and set out to stop him winning everything, since he already had an excellent pupil in Collei. In 6.6 they talked through the shared risk of the Irminsul plan. She quoted Vahumana on the insignificance of individual fates; he, from Amurta, disagreed.

2.comment: Faruzan: The Century in the Ruin
2.content:
About a hundred years ago Faruzan miscalculated while solving a puzzle in a King Deshret ruin filled with mechanisms and coded inscriptions, and was trapped. A mysterious power kept her body in stasis: no hunger, no physical fatigue, but no escape from mental wear. She used up her paper without translating a single line, then carved deductions into the floor with broken stone so the next trapped person might have a chance. When the floor was full she calculated in her head. Her memory blurred and she began muttering. At some point she solved it, though she no longer remembers how. Wind met her at the exit, and she followed it, with her new Vision, until she collapsed from hunger. A caravan found her by her glittering Vision.

In Sumeru she first believed she was still inside some illusion device. She recovered slowly; an Akademiya researcher confirmed her identity with old Akasha records and gave her a Kshahrewar book dedicated to her. Reading it, she remembered her classmates and understood they were all gone. To the nervous researcher beside her she said evenly that it was just a failed experiment. Her fallen voice lines echo it ("Time... didn't stop for me...").

Folk versions of the story had her imprisoned in the Temple of Silence for touching forbidden knowledge, or taken up to live with the gods. Matra once suspected that her silence hid something sinister, until Cyno cleared her.

3.comment: Faruzan: Tamimi and the Last Letters
3.content:
In her Hangout Event (3.5), Faruzan, the Traveler and an archaeologist named Raed found a huge machine wreck in the Hypostyle Desert. Faruzan saw that it was only about a dozen years old and decoded Raed's "excavation records", in which "tents" was code for relics he was selling. When the wreck reactivated and chased the diggers, she realised it was Tamimi, the small mechanical life form that once took her notes and carried her letters home. Her teacher and friends had rebuilt it to learn and repair itself, and it had searched the ruins for decades, growing into the legendary "Ruin Wanderer", to deliver their letters. Her mother's ends: "Welcome home, Faruzan." Tamimi's overworked heart gave out after it found her.

Faruzan stayed alone with Tamimi for a while. She then brought its parts back to Pardis Dhyai to repair Karkata. She will not give them away "for free": she means to revive Tamimi once she has replicated the ancient techniques. Depending on the player's choice, she either faces Tighnari and Collei's sympathy or asks the Traveler to keep the secret for now. On a moonlit walk she says the letters brought her family's faces back, and that she would disappoint them by falling into a slump. When the Traveler says "Welcome home, Faruzan," she answers: "Yeah, I'm home."

The letters are a teacher's note calling her "the most exceptional student I've ever met"; a junior's note promising her manuscripts would carry her name; a much-corrected note telling her to come home for a meal; and her mother's letter, written about twenty years after she vanished, when the mother sensed she had little time left. Raed's evidence went to the Akademiya. The quest awards the achievement "To You in a Hundred Years".

4.content:
Faruzan's field is "the analysis of the structure of and solutions to various ruin devices via the study of stone carvings and other ancient texts", so it is linguistics applied to mechanisms. A century ago it was vital; now Kshahrewar's mechanics have matured and few ruins remain unexplored. Haravatat reviewers reject her topics and cut her funding, and students fall asleep in her lectures. Kshahrewar, whose students graduated on her manuscripts, keeps offering better terms. One recruiter who said "the era of interpreting ancient texts is over" was lectured for the length of two classes and drank himself sorry at Lambad's Tavern. A Haravatat friend who set out to debate "this old fogey" ended up the same way the next night.

Kshahrewar students quietly come to her for remedial mechanics, bringing no gift, only humility and the word "Madam". She calls the Haravatat elders "geezers" and points out that by their logic Haravatat, the Darshan with the lowest enrolment, should close. She still turned down Kshahrewar's offer: someone has to study niche topics.

In the 3.5 hangout an administrator, Nadwah, demanded that she either teach a course or join Acara Crafts' collaboration with Kshahrewar's representative Anis. One branch produced a public reading course; another produced children's learning toys and a reference book.

5.comment: Faruzan: Cyno and the Vairambhaka Gear
5.content:
The Vairambhaka Gear, a "multi-purpose ruin exploration auxiliary support terminal", was one of the few projects the Akademiya funded after her return. Matra stormed her workshop, suspecting her silence about her disappearance and her refusal to join Kshahrewar hid a dangerous machine. General Mahamatra Cyno arrived, cleared her with records, apologised and left a matra to help tidy up. Pleased, she invited him to name the machine. He proposed "Great Vayuvyastra", which baffled her; a matra noted Kshahrewar already had a machine by that name. She studied how such names are formed and chose "Vairambhaka" herself.

She says Cyno's jokes defeat her: she tried to decode their grammar for hidden meaning and was told they are just literal meanings and homophones. In 4.6, after Cyno's group handled a desert catastrophe without her, she scolded them all for not involving an experienced senior.

6.content: Karkata is a crab-like mechanical life form at Pardis Dhyai, the last work of Tighnari's late junior Abattouy, an expelled Spantamad researcher. In the hangout Faruzan diagnosed a failing Restitution Module, an ancient self-repair design modelled on a heart, rare even a century ago, which Abattouy probably dug up in the Great Red Sand. Faruzan said that if Abattouy were still alive they could have talked all day. Karkata now runs on parts from Tamimi.

7.content: Faruzan once chatted with Kaveh about mechanism construction and found him "too much of an artsy romantic" but full of original ideas. She has promised to treat him to a good meal "once my funding gets approved". In the 3.6 Extravaganza (limited) they built mechanical butterflies together and drew lots for the points. In 6.6 she called for him to judge a sculpture because of his "excellent aesthetic tastes"; he was too busy reviewing a proposal.

8.content: Faruzan sees Layla in the library at night, where Layla waves and smiles, yet by day Layla ducks her. She concludes that Rtawahist geniuses are allowed a quirk or two. In the limited 4.4 event Receiver of Friends From Afar, Dori hired them both to tune the compass and equipment of a test cruise from Port Ormos. Faruzan took the lowest possible pay to undercut Kshahrewar competitors, for the right to buy old books at every port. At Wangshu Inn she tried to order the priciest dishes until Dori talked her out of seafood. She read the Liyue idiom in the dish's name at once, and shocked Layla by claiming students once had to master twenty languages.

9.comment: Faruzan: Nicole and the Heroic Squirrel
9.content: At the Temple of Silence during the 6.6 crisis, Nicole showed the Kshahrewar scholars a lifelike squirrel sculpture. Faruzan suggested a hero's pose with a finger raised to the heavens, "a certain classical beauty", and Nicole loved it. Faruzan said anyone who wishes may call her Madam and looked forward to Nicole's next work. Puzzled by Nicole's mention of watching over generations of heroes, she asked what Nicole did for a living. The scholars decided not to tell her.

10.content: In 6.6 Irminsul stopped processing information and Sumeru's rainforest was evacuated. The planners modified Aaru at the Temple of Silence with Kaveh, Faruzan and every mechanics scholar working full-time. Grand Sage Naphis then assigned Faruzan, Collei and Nicole to support Dori on the elemental energy amplifier. Faruzan was proud of her flawless assembly and intrigued that such a small device could output Light Realm power. Nervous before the decisive moment, she made carton after carton of juice with Collei's juicer and pressed it on everyone. The crisis ended with Irminsul burned and Aaru taking over its storage role.

11.content: During the limited 3.6 event A Parade of Providence, Faruzan nominated herself for Haravatat in the Interdarshan Championship against Tighnari, Cyno, Kaveh, Layla and the Wanderer. She wanted students and the research funding prize. She tried to recruit Layla on the spot, teamed with Kaveh on mechanical butterflies, and followed a misbehaving Primal Construct across the desert to a hidden Ley Line disruptor. She offered to dress Dehya and Candace in a "timeless classic" style of embroidered flowers on plain cloth, until Nilou politely steered them to newer fashions. Afterward a girl named Fawara asked to study under her, and she promised her the best teaching available.

12.comment: Faruzan: Fieldwise Center and the Puzzlepal
12.content: In the limited 6.1 event Ruins Exploration: Fieldwise Center, Faruzan served as a consultant at Aaru Village for the "Puzzlepal". This doll-like autonomous puzzle device, modelled on her, was built by her Haravatat juniors with the Puzzlers' League and the Synopsium on Ruin Mechanisms. She wanted a square metal casing, but gave in when the Traveler liked the cute version. She prefers refined dolls to cute ones; on automation, she thinks machines should handle repetitive work while humans keep control of judgement. After a desert feast she planned to send the Knights of Favonius Library a reading list to test "Cyrus's prized student", Lisa.

13.comment: Faruzan: Tales of Shahryar and Onibudou
13.content: In one hangout branch, Faruzan sets up a reading course for Collei and goes looking for teaching material. Light novels baffle her: titles too long, isekai logic, "dark history". She wants "Tales of Shahryar", a Vahumana researcher's serial that everyone read a century ago. She finds only volume five, a muddled late entry, and learns that the series chased trends, lost its readers and never finished, while the older "Legend of Antara" endured. Shaken, she reflects that a work should at least stay true to itself, and adopts Collei's favourite, "Onibudou", as course material.

14.content: In another hangout branch Faruzan helped Acara Crafts and Kshahrewar's Anis design children's learning toys. She sketched the "Pagoda Stack", a ring-moving puzzle from ancient ruin principles, and showed Anis that a seven-layer tower needs 127 moves. Her lesson was that a mechanism's complexity lies in its rules, not its part count. Her reference book either became ruin-safety material for adventurers, or a children's class where the children said they would join Kshahrewar. She told them the only person who can restrict a researcher's curiosity is the researcher.

15.content: Her yearly letters to the Traveler: 2023, a letter to be read only if she failed to return from a ruin in time to cancel it, with the ruin's location attached so that "this time, there will be someone who knows where to find me"; 2024, a briefing on Natlan's ancient texts for the Traveler's journey; 2025, annoyance and quiet pride that her students idolise the Traveler as a "savior"; 2026, a bucket of homemade "Ultimate Fruit & Veggie Boost" after juicing every fruit Collei brought.
